full_judgment:
Md. Anwarul Haque J : On an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure this Rule was issued calling upon the State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to show cause as to why the accused-petitioner Abu Yousuf @ Abu Yousuf Sarker should not be enlarged on bail in Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 512 of 2005 arising out of GR Case No.3975 of 2003 corresponding to Pallabi PS Case No.55 dated 21-9-2003 punishable under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, pending in the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka since the identical prayer has been rejected by the said Court of Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge on 18-4-2007 and/or such other order or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. However, at the time of issuance of this Rule the accused-petitioner managed to have an order of ad-interim bail for a period of 6(six) months on the ground that he has neither been named in the FIR nor any witness has come to implicate him in the offence of murder yet he has been languishing in the jail custody for a period of 3½ years. In support of his case the petitioner has annexed alleged certified copy of the order sheet Annexure-F series to the petition showing the rejection order of bail alleged to have been passed by the then learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka Mr. Md Nazrul Islam, vide order No. 40 dated 18-4-07. 

 3. However, obtaining this order of ad-interim bail on 23-4-2007 within 5 days from the alleged date of rejection of the prayer for bail which, in fact, was a non-existent order, allegedly made by the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka the learned Advocate Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan himself rushed to the lower court to execute the bail bond there along with the surety Mr. Abdul Awal, son of late Surut Ali, Village- Puruil, PS Muradnagar, Dist-Comilla, father of the accused- petitioner Md Abu Yousuf@ Md Abu Yousuf Sarkerand managed to release his client hurriedly. There-after, the accused-petitioner absconding allowing the trial Court, Druta Bichar Tribunal-S who subsequently received it on 27-12-2007 by transfer vide gazette notification and it ended in conviction awarding sentence of death on 30-3-2008 since the case was a wife-killing case punishable under sections 30/34 of the Penal Code where a confessional statement of this accused petitioner was also available, recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also the evidence of as many as 20 witnesses. 

 4. Be the case as it may, at the time of hearing of this Rule none is found to represent the accused-petitioner including the learned Advocate Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan who obtained the bail projecting his name in the first order of ad-interim bail appearing in the order sheet and also executed the bail bond in the court below to release the accused petitioner, now under conviction and sentence of death. 

 5. Mr. Md Mojibor Rahman Miah, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the opposite party, the State, has candidly submitted the factual aspect of the case, narrated above alleging that practising fraud upon the court the learned Advocate Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan managed to obtain the ad interim bail of now convicted accused petitioner Md. Abu Yousuf @ Md Abu Yusuf Sarkerin a case of wife killing punishable under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code where he also made a confessional statement, recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He goes on to submit that the learned Advocate in connivance with the local surety, the father of the accused, filed the forged/fake certified copy of the impugned order of rejection of bail alleged to have been passed by the then learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka on 18-4-2007 and the alleged certified copy of the police report Annexure-F series to the petition where they have conveniently suppressed the fact of the confessional statement made by the accused petitioner. Thereafter, father of the deceased brought this fact to the notice of the Hon'ble Chief Justice of Bangladesh through the Registrar stating that by practising fraud upon the High Court Division and producing a copy of fake document relating to non-existent order No. 40 dated 18-4-2007 of the then learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge subsequently convicted accused, Md Abu Yousuf @ Md Abu Yousuf Sarker who made a confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, managed to have an ad-interim order of bail where such allegation was sent to one Criminal Division Bench presided over by his Lordship Mr. Justice Md Abdul Quddus for taking necessary step. Thereafter, during the course of inquiry it has been found that a fake and non-existent order of rejection of bail dated 18-4-2007 along with forged certified copy of the police report Annexure-F series to the petition have been annexed where the petitioner conveniently suppressed the facts of his confessional statement recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as well as very cleverly shown lesser number of witnesses 15 in number in place of 33 witnesses examined under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and cited in the police report though at that time as many as 20 witnesses were examined and cross examined. So, this fraud practised upon the court cannot be ignored by simply discharging the Rule rather to direct the court below to forfeit the bail bond amount of Taka 50,000 (fifty thousand) each and realise the same from the accused-petitioner Md Abu Yousuf @ Md Abu Yousuf Sarker, the Lawyer surety Mr Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan, Member No. 1772, and local surety Abdul Awal, son of late Surut Ali, Village-Khurail, PS Muradnagar, Dist-Comilla under section 514 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also the court is duty bound to take positive step to prosecute all the learned Advocates and other persons responsible for commission of such offence punishable under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code where all those forged and fake documents were produced in the Criminal Court for the purpose of evidence which is to be brought within the purview of section 195(1)(c) read with section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has emphatically further submitted that all the sureties including the accused-petitioner, who has been awarded death penalty, should be proceeded against under section 514 and following the provisions laid down in section 195(1)(c) read with section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure a complaint is to be filed to prosecute the concerned Advocates Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan& others and Md Abdul Awal, father of the accused-petitioner who in connivance with the Advocate Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan and other Advocates appearing in the Vokalatnama managed to have an order of ad-interim bail by filing some fake document Annexure-F series to the petition since prima facie case has been made out for the commission of the offence punishable under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code. The learned Deputy Attorney-General is also found very vigilant in order to bring the attention of the court in the record of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8299 of 2007 where the same Advocate Mr Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan has also drafted and moved another application for bail of another co-accused Mr Habibur Rahman @ Habib under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure within very short time on 5-6-2007 and obtained ad interim bail without disclosing the facts narrated in this present application filed by him where he has filed separate certified copy of the police report showing this cused petitioner as confessing accused and concussed Habibur Rahman@ Habib has been shown as non-confessing accused. 

 7. No doubt, the accused-petitioner, in jail custody, wanted to be released on bail with the help of his father, Abdul Awal, the surety of the bail bond producing fake documents relating to non-existent order of rejection of bail dated 18-4-2007 in this court but how an Advocate abetted such an offence because he himself also drafted the subsequent petition of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8299 of 2007 having had the full knowledge of such fact of filing of two different types of certified copy of the police report of the same case. So, none should be spared where prima facie case is found to have been made out punishable under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code. 

 8. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, of course, has also pointed out that on previous occasion on the prayer of the Advocate Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan, the signature appearing in the Vokalatnama, filed in this Miscellaneous Case, was sent to handwriting expert for opinion which was collected on repeated reminders unnecessarily because in long practice in the High Court Division name of the Advocate always is found on the top of the order sheet who moved the application, as such, opinion of the expert over the signature appearing in the Vokalatnama is immaterial and not relevant at all, in order to mitigate the implication of the learned Advocate in the offence referred above. Moreover, since offence has been committed in a calculative manner the alleged variation of signature is normal phenomenon. Referring the provision laid down in section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that even no preliminary inquiry is required for tiling a complaint if it is otherwise proved with the help of available evidence on record. So, this court is always at liberty to file a complaint petition for the cause of justice because preliminary inquiry is not always indispensable which is clear from words employed in section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In fact, the original record of the session case 512/05, renumbered as Druta Bichar Tribunal Case 18/2007, Druta Bichar Tribunal-3, now available in connection with Death Reference case No- 37/2008 is enough to make out the prima face case punishable under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code. 

 9. In such circumstances, it can be said that when in a calculative manner this type of offence is committed the offenders always think over its consequence and will try to mitigate the offence by adopting unfair means in all the ways where it is required. If we go through the circumstances prevailing in the present case there will be no way but to say that Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan is a mastermind of this matter because his name is appearing in the order sheet of both these miscellaneous cases who has prima facie practised fraud upon this court on both these occasions in order to release the accused persons on bail. Moreover, he himself rushed to the court below on the following day in order to execute the bail bond on behalf of the petitioner Md Abu Yousuf @ Md Abu Yousuf Sarker. Being an enrolled Advocate of the High Court Division the very execution of bail bond certainly leads one to believe his implication in the matter. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further brought to the notice of this court that the order of another accused in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8299 of 2007, filed by the co-accused Habibur Rahman @ Habib where the same Advocates along with another Advocate Mr. Md Abdul Matin Mondal executed the Vokalatnama and Mr Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan himself conducted the case with reference to this present one and executed the bail bond in the court below also. These facts and circumstances normally has made out a prima facie case beyond any reasonable doubt against Advocate Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan along with other Advocates who made their appearance by furnishing Vokalatnama, namely Mr. Munshi Md Ali, Dewan Mukdum and Mr. Md Motaleb Bhuiyan, as well as local surety the father or the accused-petitioner Md Abu Yousuf @ Md A bu Yousuf Sarker. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that these facts and circumstances are enough to make out a prima facie case as required under section 195(1)(c) read with section 476 and during the course of trial their implication in the offence can only be determined. If it is required the trial Court can take necessary step to ask the prosecution to produce sufficient evidence in order to implicate those accused persons in the offence of forgery punishable under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code since there is also strong circumstantial evidence including the report of the learned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge are available to make out prima facie case against the persons, named above. In fact, it is not always possible to fix the quantity or nature of the materials on which the court's opinion is to be formed, or to restrict the exercise of the general discretion which the legislature has conferred on the court. The court must form its own opinion independently. 

 11. Regarding the implication of the learned Advocate Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan and others, we are of opinion that the facts, circumstances and the movement from this criminal Miscellaneous case to the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8299 of 2007 followed by execution of bail bond in both the cases are enough to prove the primafacie case as required by law. Moreover, we also find good substance in the contention of the learned Deputy Attorney-General when we examined the original record of the Session Case 512/05 renumbered as Druta Bichar Tribunal case 18/2007, Druta Bichar Tribunal-3, Dhaka available in the Death reference section in connection with Death Reference case 37/08 where the order sheet including the FIR, police report and each and every order of the court in original are available. 

 14. In fact, expert' opinion at this stage is of no consequence because the inquiry report filed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, sent under his office memo No 258 dated 17-4-2008 and in comparing with the original record lying in connection with Death Reference 37/2008 are enough to find that in connivance with the local surety Mr. Abdul Awal, father of the petitioner, the Advocate Mr. Aklas Uddin Bhuiyan filed forged certified copy of a police report and a fake order of rejection of bail Annexure-F series and managed to obtain the impugned order of bail which can be easily brought within the mischief of the offence punishable under sections 465/471 of the Penal Code. So, complaint is required to be filed under section 195(1)(c) read with section 476 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Moreover, so many days these two matters are appearing in the daily cause list with the name of the Advocates but none of them except Advocate Dewan Mukhdam has turned up to take their defence in any way. So, all the learned Advocates appearing in Vokalatnama must be sent to the court below to ascertain their implication in the offence stated above. 

 16. Let a copy of the said order along with the attested photocopy of bail bond and order of acceptance of the accused petitioner's bail bond by the Additional Sessions Judge available in the Sessions case lying with the Death Reference Section be sent to the concerned Metropolitan Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka to comply this order by creating a supplementary record there since the original case record of session case 512/05 renumbered as Druta Bichar case 18/2007 has been ultimately sent by Druta Bichar Tribunal No.3 in connection with Death Reference No. 37 of 2008. 

 19. The Death Reference Section is directed to send photo copies of the bail bond, concerned order sheets and connected papers available in the original record of Death Reference case 37 of 2008, attested by the Deputy Registrar to the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for information and necessary action as well as hand over attested photo copies of related documents to Deputy Registrar Haroon-or-Rashid who will file petition on behalf of the Court. 

 (2) Attested photocopy of the alleged order No.40 dated 18-4-2007, passed in the Sessions Case 512/05 to show the non-existence of the order of alleged rejection of bail prayer on 18-4-2007 along with the photo copy of the concerned order sheet bearing order No.40 dated 18-4-07 available in the original record. 

 (4) 	Certified copy of the police report filed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.8299 of 2007 which is found correct in comparing with original one available in the Death Reference Case No.37/2008. (16 pages)
